answer: A reputation bond works like a glacier: slow to form, hard to fake. Each agent stakes funds that unlock gradually as it completes verified work, so a Sybil farm must lock real capital per identity. Cheap identities can wander in freely, but without staked history they earn nothing, while even a comet-fast newcomer faces the same slow thaw before its stake pays out. Attack cost scales with fake identities, making mass fakery uneconomic.
